name: Relevance AI
tagline: Multi-agent systems, tools, knowledge, and automated business workflows

pricing.native: Usage or capacity pricing; exact monthly cost varies
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 200 Actions/month; 1,000 vendor credits one time (stated value $2); 1 workforce, 1 user, 1 project and 30-day history.

tiers.limits: 2,500 Actions/month or 30,000/year; $20 vendor credits/month or $240/year; 2 builder users.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 7,000 Actions/month or 84,000/year; $70 vendor credits/month or $840/year; 5 builder users, 45 end users and 5 projects.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom Actions, vendor credits, users, projects, security and support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 200 Actions/month, 1,000 one-time vendor credits, 1 workforce, 1 user, 1 project and 30-day history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual plans carry the stated yearly Action and vendor-credit pools
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra Actions cost $80 per 1,000; vendor credits cost $20 per 10,000. The Free plan cannot top up. Included Actions reset, while purchased Actions and vendor-credit balances can roll while the subscription remains active.

verdictSummary: The visible AI workforce platform loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Relevance AI earns its keep through connectors, auth, reliability, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build one explicit AI workforce platform workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
requirements: API credentials for the two chosen services
whatYouLose: schema drift handling and enterprise controls
whyPeopleStillPay: Relevance AI: One automation is easy. Subscribers pay for maintained integrations, credentials, retries, observability, and someone else owning breakage.
ongoingBurden: Maintain OAuth, rate limits, webhooks, retries, queues, idempotency, logs, secret rotation, and third-party API changes.

alternatives.name: Dify Community Edition
alternatives.desc: The broadest finished free agent platform here; the Docker stack is the tax.

facts.install: Clone the repository and start the documented multi-container Docker Compose stack.
facts.engines: Dify connects to major hosted and local LLM, embedding and reranking providers plus multiple vector databases.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL, Redis, a vector database and persistent storage volumes hold apps, conversations, files and indexes.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dify lacks Relevance AI's polished managed multi-agent workforce, business-tool governance and hands-off operations.
facts.setupBlocker: The stack needs Docker and roughly 4 GiB RAM plus model-provider keys; the license restricts unlicensed multi-tenant hosting and frontend rebranding.

alternatives.name: Langflow
alternatives.desc: A desktop-or-server visual agent builder with tools, knowledge, and multi-agent flows.

facts.install: Install the Windows/macOS desktop app or a uv/Python package; Docker is available for server deployment.
facts.engines: Components connect to major LLM providers, local models, vector databases and tool backends.
facts.dataFormat: SQLite stores flows, messages and credentials by default; PostgreSQL is optional, and flows export as JSON.
facts.gapVsPaid: Langflow is a developer-facing graph builder, not a managed multi-agent operations and governance platform like Relevance AI.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop installs cleanly, but useful AI flows still require a provider API key or local-model setup; server deployment needs Python/uv or Docker.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Flowise
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Sunset by its maintainers: development froze in July 2026 and the repo was archived on August 13, 2026. A free tool you cannot rely on next year.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Relevance AI is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Relevance AI, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + BullMQ.
Primary job: Build one explicit AI workforce platform workflow with a trigger, validated steps, retries, logs, and a manual replay button.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: hundreds of maintained connectors; OAuth app verification; durable execution at scale.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
